Whether you’re a seasoned game dev, a designer, an artist, a sound person, or someone who has never shipped a game before, you’re welcome. Bring a laptop, bring friends, or find your team on the night.

We want games that make the room come alive! Think shouting, laughing, moving around, friendly competition, and unforgettable moments. The kind of gameplay that’s so entertaining people can’t resist pulling out their phones to share it on Instagram Stories, Snapchat, or TikTok.
The winning team will be invited to pitch their game to Weekend’s product and engineering teams and get feedback from the people behind our growing portfolio of TV games!
Random Games Track:
Anything goes. Platformers, puzzlers, roguelikes, narrative experiments, cozy sims, or something nobody has a genre name for yet. If it’s fun, surprising, and fits the theme, it belongs here.

WHAT IS re:AGENT

re:AGENT is a two-day build weekend focused on the infrastructure scientific agents still need: better datasets, sharper tools, and reliable ways to evaluate their work. Participants will use Paperclip , Proto , Claude , and other scientific AI tools to build systems that can take on real scientific problems and produce results worth trusting.
Paperclip turns papers, datasets, clinical trials, and biological databases into an agent-native workspace that AI systems can search, synthesize, and build upon. Proto is a design framework and infrastructure layer for generative biology, allowing builders to combine AI models and search for DNA, RNA, or protein sequences that satisfy custom criteria.
The weekend brings together engineers, scientists, computational biologists, founders, and AI researchers. Projects might include assembling a research-ready dataset that would be impractical to create by hand, along with the analysis needed to show that its findings are real. Others might involve designing a new biological system to a defined specification and testing whether it holds up against existing evidence.
The aim is not just to accelerate existing workflows, but to create the tools, datasets, and evaluation methods that make entirely new scientific questions and experiments possible.

About Event

MakerMods Physical AI Hacks 🤖
This is the best Physical AI hackathon you've been looking for.

Join MakerMods and Dream Labs on November 7–8 at Founders Inc. in San Francisco for a weekend of building physical AI: robots that act on the world, agents that coordinate those actions, and applications that bring the two together.
We’re bringing bimanual 6-axis robot arms, Dream Labs’ Dream-1, and a target of 200 builders into one space. Bring your ideas, your teammates, and a willingness to debug something that can actually move.
Brough to you by:
MakerMods
MakerMods is a full-stack robotics company making Physical AI accessible to everyone. We build affordable robot hardware and software that lets people teach robots to do physical tasks—from makers experimenting at home to researchers building the next generation of robot intelligence. Built for makers, by makers.
Dream Labs
Dream Labs is bringing “everyday capabilities to everyday robots.” Its robot brain, Dream-1, is built to work across different robots, tasks, and environments. Through the Dream API, developers can turn camera observations and task instructions into robot actions, and adapt the model with their own demonstrations.

Two ways to build

One challenge. One leaderboard.
Take on a shared, long horizon Physical AI tasks using our Metal Arm stations.
Your team's rank is based only on your eval score.
No pitching. No larping. It's all skill based.
You’ll collect demonstrations and fine-tune the lastest SOTA World Action Model by Dream Labs: Dream-1. Then your team builds the harness around the model: deciding what happens next, checking whether an action worked, and recovering when it didn’t.
The same Dream-1 model can produce very different results depending on the fine-tuning data and the harness you build around it.
Can your robot finish the task? Can it recover from a failed attempt? Can you push your score higher before the deadline?
Scores come from task performance against published rules. Leading teams will make scored attempts live on stage while the competition continues at the other stations.
The full challenge and scoring rules will be shared before the event.
💡 Creative Applications (Track 2) What would you build if your agent had robot arms?
Build an application around Dream-1 and our Maker Arm stations.
Connect robot actions to voice, agents, human input, and everyday tools. Make something useful, surprising, playful—or something nobody in the room would have thought to try.
Some directions to explore:
A voice-controlled assistant that asks for help when it gets stuck.

A robot workflow triggered by a calendar event or a message.

An interactive experience where people and robots solve something together.

A physical tool your software agent can call to get a real-world job done.

Book robot time, bring your own props or work creatively with the materials available, and film your project in action.
Three finalists will pitch on stage with their demo videos. A judging panel will select first, second, and third place.
Creative awards are judged separately from the hill-climb leaderboard, with the rubric published beforehand.

Robot-learning researchers. ML engineers. Agent builders. Hardware hackers. Students. Designers with an idea that needs to exist outside a screen.
You don’t need to arrive as a robotics expert. Teams will need different strengths: collecting demonstrations, building agents, integrating tools, designing interactions, and making the whole stack work. Workshops from MakerMods, Dream Labs and more sponsors will help you get familiar with frontier Physical AI robotics hardware and world action models.
If you’ve been looking for a reason to try physical AI on real hardware, this is it.

Shared access to real bimanual robot stations.

Dream-1 access for building and running your projects.

An opening setup workshop to help teams get started.

A weekend of building alongside people working across robotics and AI.

Live robot attempts, creative project pitches, and awards across both tracks.

Robot time will be booked and shared across teams. Plan to use time away from the arms for coding, reviewing data, and improving your application.

Bring your laptop and charger. For creative projects, you’re welcome to bring props; we’ll share setup and hardware guidance before the event.

A text box only catches what a student types. A great teacher notices much more: the pause before a hard word, the crossed-out step in a math problem, the moment a class goes quiet. Build quick, fair, automated ways to understand where a learner is, using voice, handwriting, and interaction instead of long one-on-one tests.
Ideas: a reading-fluency screener that listens to a child read aloud · early dyslexia signals from speech and spelling · a math-fluency check from handwritten work · teacher-ready reports that turn results into next steps
🃏 Wildcard (Open Category)
Any multi-modal idea that doesn't fit the tracks above. If it solves a real problem in learning and shows a measurable learning outcome, build it.

What if you could build an AI application that works, even when the Wi-Fi doesn't?
Your flight is preparing for takeoff. Once the cabin doors close, your connection to the cloud disappears. Before switching to airplane mode, you have one mission: build an AI project that runs entirely on-device.

Unlike traditional AI applications that depend on cloud servers, on-device AI runs models directly on the user's hardware. That means your product can benefit from:
Low latency ⚡

Greater user privacy 🔒

No server inference costs 💸

Offline functionality 📴
